title: 11th Word: Construction of the Palace and Appointment of the Explaining Master

questions.question: What big project did the king begin to make for his purpose?
questions.answer: He began building a huge and beautiful palace.

questions.question: How did the king make the palace beautiful inside?
questions.answer: He filled it with precious things, fine decorations, and skillful artwork.

questions.question: What did the king prepare after the palace was finished?
questions.answer: He prepared large tables full of many kinds of food and blessings.

questions.question: How were the tables arranged for the guests?
questions.answer: Each group was given a table that suited it.

questions.question: Who was invited to come to the palace?
questions.answer: The king invited people and subjects from all parts of his land.

questions.question: What were the guests supposed to do at the palace besides eat?
questions.answer: They were supposed to look at the display and understand what it meant.

questions.question: Why did the king appoint a highest-ranking teacher?
questions.answer: He appointed him to explain the palace, its maker, its decorations, and the right way to behave there.

questions.question: What help did the main teacher have in the palace?
questions.answer: He had assistants in every section of the palace.

questions.question: Where did the main teacher stay while teaching?
questions.answer: He stayed in the biggest room with his students.

questions.question: What kinds of things was the teacher supposed to explain about the palace decorations?
questions.answer: He was supposed to explain their secrets, what they pointed to, and how they showed the owner’s greatness and skill.

questions.question: What else was the teacher told to teach the visitors about behavior?
questions.answer: He was to teach the proper way to view everything and the ceremonies the king wanted.

questions.question: What was the palace like in size and beauty?
questions.answer: It was very large, grand, and richly decorated.

questions.question: What did the king use from his own wealth to decorate the palace?
questions.answer: He used valuable treasures and beautiful crafted works.

questions.question: Why did the king make different tables for different groups?
questions.answer: He wanted each group to have what fit them properly.

questions.question: What two main things were visitors meant to do in the palace?
questions.answer: They were meant to enjoy the blessings and learn from what they saw.

questions.question: Why was one teacher not enough by himself for the whole palace?
questions.answer: The palace had many areas, so helpers were needed in each place.

questions.question: Why did the king need someone to tell people about the palace’s maker?
questions.answer: The visitors would not understand the real meaning on their own.

questions.question: What were the jewels and decorations supposed to help people notice?
questions.answer: They were supposed to help people notice the owner’s excellence, wisdom, and art.

questions.question: Why were the official ceremonies important?
questions.answer: They showed the respectful way the king wanted people to act.

questions.question: What happened after the teacher gathered with his students in the biggest room?
questions.answer: He made an announcement to all the people watching.

questions.question: What did the king do first in carrying out his plan?
questions.answer: He built a great palace.

questions.question: Into what did the king divide the palace?
questions.answer: He divided it into splendid rooms and living spaces.

questions.question: How was the palace connected to the king’s own abilities?
questions.answer: It was decorated and arranged by the king’s own treasures, art, wisdom, and knowledge.

questions.question: What was placed on the broad tables in the palace?
questions.answer: Many delicious foods and many kinds of blessings were placed there.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the banquet by saying it seemed to come through many arts?
questions.answer: It suggests the banquet was prepared with amazing care, skill, and planning.

questions.question: From where did the invited people come?
questions.answer: They came from every region of the king’s lands.

questions.question: What was one job of the teacher in explaining the palace contents?
questions.answer: He had to explain what the things inside meant.

questions.question: What was one job of the teacher in relation to the palace owner?
questions.answer: He had to describe the maker and show the owner’s qualities through the palace.

questions.question: What was one job of the teacher in relation to the visitors?
questions.answer: He had to teach them the right manners and ceremonies.

questions.question: Why is it important that the king did not appear directly?
questions.answer: It made the teacher necessary to explain what the king wanted.

questions.question: What does the use of assistants in every area tell us about the teaching in the palace?
questions.answer: It shows the teaching was organized and meant to reach everyone throughout the palace.

questions.question: What details show that the palace was not plain or simple?
questions.answer: It had magnificent rooms, precious decorations, and finely made works.

questions.question: What does the passage show about the king’s personal role in the palace’s beauty?
questions.answer: He personally adorned it with great artistry.

questions.question: Why were the food tables an important part of the palace?
questions.answer: They showed generosity and gave blessings for the guests to enjoy.

questions.question: What does the phrase about each group having a fitting table help us understand?
questions.answer: It helps us understand that the arrangements were thoughtful and suitable for different people.

questions.question: Why did the king invite people from all over his kingdom instead of only one place?
questions.answer: He wanted many of his people to benefit from the feast and see the display.

questions.question: What was the teacher supposed to reveal about the decorations and designs?
questions.answer: He was supposed to reveal their hidden meanings and what they pointed toward.

questions.question: How would the teacher help visitors connect the palace to its owner?
questions.answer: He would show how the palace’s beauty and order reflected the owner’s perfection and skill.

questions.question: What kind of guidance about actions did the teacher give, not just guidance about ideas?
questions.answer: He gave guidance about proper behavior and formal conduct.

questions.question: What does the teacher’s place in the largest room suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests he was the central guide for the people there.

questions.question: What happened right before the teacher spoke to everyone?
questions.answer: He remained with his students in the largest room while his assistants were spread through the palace.

questions.question: What can you say about the palace from the way it was built and decorated?
questions.answer: It was made with great beauty, order, and careful skill.

questions.question: What kinds of things from the king’s own stores were used in the palace?
questions.answer: Precious jewels and other valuable treasures were used.

questions.question: How do we know the king wanted the guests to feel honored?
questions.answer: He prepared rich tables, arranged them carefully, and invited people from everywhere.

questions.question: Why is the banquet described in such a rich and impressive way?
questions.answer: To show the king’s generosity and the amazing care put into what was offered.

questions.question: What was the teacher meant to make known about the palace itself?
questions.answer: He was meant to make known its purpose, meanings, and secrets.

questions.question: What was the teacher meant to make known about the palace owner?
questions.answer: He was meant to help people know the maker through what was in the palace.

questions.question: What was the teacher meant to explain about the jewelry and patterns?
questions.answer: He was meant to explain what they represented and how they showed the owner’s excellence.

questions.question: What role did the assistants play in the teaching mission?
questions.answer: They helped spread guidance through every part of the palace.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the teacher’s overall job?
questions.answer: His overall job was to help people understand the palace, its owner, and the right way to act there.

questions.question: What happened after all these arrangements were made?
questions.answer: The teacher addressed all the spectators.

questions.question: What did the king build in order to carry out his plan?
questions.answer: He built a grand and spacious palace.

questions.question: What three main features filled the palace according to the passage?
questions.answer: It had splendid rooms, precious decorations, and beautiful crafted works.

questions.question: How was wisdom shown in the way the palace was arranged?
questions.answer: Everything was organized with very fine and careful artistry.

questions.question: How was knowledge shown in the palace?
questions.answer: It was shown through remarkable and skillful works throughout the palace.

questions.question: What was special about the food prepared in the palace?
questions.answer: It included many kinds of delicious food and generous gifts.

questions.question: What does it mean that the king invited subjects from all regions?
questions.answer: It means the invitation was wide and meant for all parts of his kingdom.

questions.question: Name two things the teacher had to explain to the guests.
questions.answer: He had to explain the meanings of what was inside and the proper way to behave.

questions.question: What did the teacher help people understand about the decorations?
questions.answer: He helped them understand that the decorations pointed to the owner’s qualities and skill.

questions.question: Why were assistants placed in each area of the palace?
questions.answer: So guidance could reach people throughout the whole palace.

questions.question: What was the teacher about to do at the very end of the target passage?
questions.answer: He was about to announce his message to all the people watching.
